questions.q: A particle is projected with velocity ${v}_{0}$ along $x$-axis. The deceleration on the particle is proportional to the square of the distance from the origin $i.e.a = - x^{2}$. The distance at which particle stops is -

Given initial velocity = v0

final velocity = 0

$a = - x^{2}$

now we know that $a = \dfrac{\text{dv}}{\text{dt}}$ and $\text{v} = \dfrac{\text{dx}}{\text{dt}}$

thus $\text{a} = \dfrac{\text{dv}}{\text{dt}} = \dfrac{\text{dv}}{\text{dt}} \cdot \dfrac{\text{dx}}{\text{dx}} = \dfrac{\text{vdv}}{\text{dx}}$

$\dfrac{\text{vdv}}{\text{dx}} = - x^{2}$

$\text{vdv} = - x^{2} \text{dx}$

integrating we get

$\mathop{∫}_{\text{v} 0}^{0} \text{vdv} = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{x} - x^{2} \text{dx}$

${\left(\dfrac{v^{2}}{2}\right)}_{\text{v} 0}^{0} = - {\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}\right]}_{0}^{x}$

$- \dfrac{{v}_{0}^{2}}{2} = - \dfrac{x^{3}}{3} ⇒ \text{x} = \left(\dfrac{3 {v}_{0}^{2}}{2}\right) \dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform electric field and a uniform magnetic field exist in a region in the same direction. An electron is projected with a velocity pointed in the same direction. Then the electron will be
options: Be deflected to the left without increase in speed
Be deflected to the right without increase in speed
Not be deflected but its speed will decrease
Not be deflected but its speed will increase
questions.solution: As the electron is moving parallel to both the fields, so magnetic force does not affect the electron's motion. But electric force $( qE )$ acts opposite to the motion of the electron. Hence, the electron will not be deflected but its speed will decrease.

questions.q: The magnitude of $x$ and $y$ components of $\overset{→}{A}$ are $7$ and $6$ respectively. Also, the magnitudes of $x$ and $y$ components of $\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B}$ are $11$ and $9$ respectively. Calculate the magnitude of vector $\overset{→}{B}$.
questions.solution:
Given, $\overset{→}{A} = 7\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}$

Let $\overset{→}{B} = {b}_{1}\overset{^}{i} + {b}_{2}\overset{^}{j}$ ......(i)

Given that, $\overset{→}{A} + \overset{→}{B} = 11\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j}$

Or $\left(7 + {b}_{1}\right)\overset{^}{i} + \left(6 + {b}_{2}\right)\overset{^}{j} = 11\overset{^}{i} + 9\overset{^}{j}$

Comparing the scalar component of $\overset{^}{i} and \overset{^}{j}$

$7 + {b}_{1} = 11 and 6 + {b}_{2} = 9$

$⇒ {b}_{1} = 4 and {b}_{2} = 3$

$∴$ From Equation. (i),

$\overset{→}{B} = 4\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j}$

$\left|\overset{→}{B}\right| = \sqrt{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{25} = 5$

$

$\text{w} = {∫}_a^{b}{f}_{x}\text{dx} + \mathop{∫}_b^{e}{f}_{y}\text{dy} + \mathop{∫}_c^{f}{f}_{z}\text{dz}$

Now $\mathop{∫}_a^{d} {f}_{x} \text{dx}$ is positive since ${f}_{x} > 0$ and d > a

$\mathop{∫}_b^{e} {f}_{y} \text{dy}$ in negative since ${f}_{y} > 0 ; \text{e} < \text{b}$

$\mathop{∫}_c^{f} {f}_{z} \text{dz}$ is negative ${f}_{z} < 0 \text{;} \text{f} > \text{c}$

$∴ \text{w} = {A}_{1} - {A}_{2} - {A}_{3}$

questions.q: There are two forces each having same magnitude $10\text{N}\text{.}$ One is inclined at an angle of ${30}^{o}$ and other is inclined at an angle of ${135}^{o}$ to the positive direction of $x$ -axis. The $x$ and $y$ components of the resultant are
questions.solution:
After resolving forces in $xy -$ direction, we get
Along $x$ direction, net force;
${F}_{x} = 10\left[cos{30}^{o} + \left(- cos{45}^{o}\right)\right] = 10\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 1.59\text{N}$
Along $y$ direction, net force;
${F}_{y} = 10 \left(\text\sin{30}^{o} +10\text\sin{45}^{o}\right)
${F}_{y} = 10( $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} )
$= 12.07N$
Thus forces in $x$ and $y$ direction are 1.59\text{N} and 12.07\text{N}$ respectively.

questions.solution:
$P + Q = 16$ (i)

$P^{2} + Q^{2} + 2PQcos\text{\theta} = 64$ (ii)

tan${90}^{ο} = \dfrac{Q sin \text{\theta}}{P + Q cos \text{\theta}}$



$⇒ P + Q cos \text{\theta} = 0$

$cos \text{\theta} = - \dfrac{\text{P}}{\text{Q}}$

From Eq. (ii)

$P^{2} + Q^{2} + \text{2.P.Q} \left(- \dfrac{P}{Q}\right) = \text{64}$

$- P^{2} + Q^{2} = \text{64}$

$as P + Q = 16$

$Q - P = 4$
